# Tin Fonders medgrundare om tuffa perioden – och vägen framåt

**Feed**: dagen-med-di  
**Published**: 2026-11-10  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Carl Armfelt, co-founder of TIN Fonder, explains the fund house's restructuring: assets under management have fallen sharply, CIO Henrik Kahlman is leaving and co-founder Erik Sprinchorn is stepping back from portfolio management. He points to a recent turnaround in performance and sentiment for software, medtech and Swedish small caps. On markets, he favours software, cybersecurity and medtech over AI hardware and neoclouds, which he thinks face tougher short-term conditions. He likes hyperscalers Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon, plus Swedish and Nordic holdings Yubico, Chemometec and Genovis, and is sceptical of Anthropic's valuation given falling token prices.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 YUBICO — Yubico | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Guest holding; strong report with guidance of faster growth in the coming period; cybersecurity is the top theme for next year.

#### Reasoning

Guest (TIN co-founder) holds Yubico and stresses that its post-summer report points to faster growth ahead, not just one good quarter. This fits his view that cybersecurity will be the theme every board discusses next year, even if AI capex moderates.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth guidance is not delivered
- if cybersecurity sentiment fades
- if Swedish small-cap tech sentiment reverses

> *"Det var inte ett kvartal som gick bra utan det var bolag som nu säger att de kommer att växa snabbare under en kommande period."*

---

### 🟢 CHEMM — Chemometec | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Guest holding; reverse profit warning; medtech going back to normal after a tough Trump-era period.

#### Reasoning

Guest holds Chemometec and cites its reverse profit warning as evidence of a medtech recovery. He sees the start of a long-term trend as hospital investment budgets normalise and AI drives more drug development, which needs lab equipment.

#### Sell Triggers

- if US healthcare policy turns hostile again
- if hospital capex budgets stay depressed
- if growth momentum fades

> *"Även ett kemametrik omvänd vinstvarning. Så back to normal inom medtech"*

---

### 🟢 GENO — Genovis | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Incredibly strong report, 34% growth, best since TIN became a shareholder; stock up 10.5%.

#### Reasoning

Guest is a long-time shareholder and calls today's report the best he has seen from Genovis. It supports his medtech turnaround thesis, and he says medtech is where TIN is digging most right now after cybersecurity.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth decelerates sharply
- if medtech sentiment reverses on US policy

> *"jag tycker Genovis idag otroligt stark rapport. Växer 34&nbspps. Det är den bästa rapport jag sett från dem sedan vi blev aktieägare för några år sedan."*

---

### 🟢 MSFT — Microsoft | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 75%

TIN holds it; hyperscalers seen as most win-win in big tech; disciplined AI capex scaling.

#### Reasoning

Hyperscalers combine operating cash flow with debt and sell capacity to AI labs. In an AI winter they would buy assets cheaply, and in a middle scenario they profit from selling capacity. Microsoft's report showed capex discipline. The guest says Microsoft and Alphabet feel very good.

#### Sell Triggers

- if capex discipline is abandoned
- if AI capacity demand collapses without an offset

> *"Microsoft och Alphabet känns väldigt bra."*

---

### 🟢 GOOGL — Alphabet | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 75%

TIN holds it; attractive mix of growth, valuation and AI/non-AI revenue despite Q3 capex criticism.

#### Reasoning

Guest sees Alphabet as one of the hyperscalers best placed whatever the AI outcome. It was punished in Q3 over capex, but its valuation and combined AI and non-AI revenue make it very attractive to him.

#### Sell Triggers

- if capex keeps rising without ROI discipline
- if AI demand weakens materially

> *"Microsoft och Alphabet känns väldigt bra."*

---

### 🟢 AMZN — Amazon | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

TIN's latest addition, bought during last week's turbulence after Q3 capex criticism.

#### Reasoning

Guest added Amazon as the fund's most recent holding during the sell-off. He groups it with the hyperscalers that win under most AI scenarios through capacity sales and diversified revenue.

#### Sell Triggers

- if capital prudence does not improve
- if cloud capacity demand drops

> *"Och även Amazon som faktiskt är det sista innehavet som vi la till här nu när det var riktigt stökigt förra veckan."*

---

### ⛔ CRWV — CoreWeave | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 50%

Neoclouds built out with debt alone; guest expects much tougher short-term conditions for neocloud and hardware.

#### Reasoning

Guest argues that neoclouds financed only by debt, and AI hardware generally, have worse risk-reward right now as the market pushes hyperscalers to rein in capex. CoreWeave is named as a capacity buyer, not explicitly as a stock call, so the signal is inferred and weak.

#### Sell Triggers

- if hyperscaler capex re-accelerates
- if a large drawdown makes valuation attractive (guest would 'hugga lite')

> *"Men för neo cloud och för hårdvara så blir det kortsiktigt mycket, mycket tuffare."*

---
